name: Minar Rahman

global_influences.evidence: Minar's debut album Danpitey (2008), entirely self-written, composed and performed, is credited with introducing a blend of indie, folk and alternative pop at a time when these genres were rarely explored in Bangladesh's mainstream music industry, indicating direct absorption of global indie-pop songwriting conventions.

local_adaptation_notes: A self-taught singer-songwriter inspired by his father, Minar built his career on entirely self-produced solo albums (writing, composing, and performing all material himself from his 2008 debut), a distinctly independent/DIY model within Bangladeshi pop; his collaboration with Tahsan on the arrangement of breakout hit 'Shada' also illustrates cross-artist collaboration within the Pop genre's small circle of singer-songwriter-producers.
sound_evolution_summary: Breakthrough period (2008): debut solo album Danpitey introduced a fresh indie/folk/alternative-pop identity, self-written and self-performed. Consolidation period (2011–2015): Aari (2011) and Aha Re (2015) extended this sound; 'Shada' (arranged with Tahsan) drove mainstream breakthrough, followed by highly viewed hits 'Jhoom' and 'Keu Kotha Rakheni.' Later period: continued output alongside parallel careers as a cartoonist (Unmad magazine, since 2008) and novelist (debut novel, 2019).

listener_community_notes: Represents a distinctive singer-songwriter node within the Pop genre, appealing to listeners drawn to indie/folk-inflected, self-authored songwriting rather than producer-driven or dance-oriented pop; his songs rank among the most-viewed Bangladeshi tracks on YouTube, indicating strong digital-era listener reach.
